newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER - SPOTLIGHT, NOT FLOODLIGHT FALLS ON MATCH THAT NEVER WAS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER - SPOTLIGHT, NOT FLOODLIGHT FALLS ON MATCH THAT NEVER WAS.

text.p: While 15 World Cup qualifiers in Europe served up their usual drama on Wednesday, a match that was not played stole the spotlight and earned what will be a lasting place in soccer folklore.

Minnows Estonia, never likely to achieve much on the field, failed to take the field for their scheduled group four qualifier against Scotland who went through the technicality of kicking off against absent opponents before the match was abandoned after three seconds.

The farce in Tallinn arose because Scotland, with FIFA's backing, asked for the kick-off time to be brought forward nearly three hours because of the poor standard of temporary floodlighting in the stadium.

Although the kick-off was agreed in advance between all the necessary officials and FIFA, Estonian team officials claimed they could not get the team from their training ground to the stadium in time, could not ensure security or get TV schedules altered.
As a result they failed to turn up for the match and are now likely to incur the wrath of FIFA who will almost certainly rule on November 7 that Scotland are awarded the tie 3-0.

However, UEFA president Lennart Johansson, a FIFA vice-president, said on Swedish TV: "Based on the facts I have, I think the match should be replayed. That would be best for all the parties involved."
In matches that did go ahead as scheduled European champions Germany overcame the loss of seven injured players to brush Armenia aside 5-1 in a group nine qualifier in Yerevan.

Germany, playing their first qualifying match, showed they have lost none of their power with a succession of goals from Thomas Haessler (20th and 39th minutes), skipper Juergen Klinsmann (26th), Fredi Bobic (69th) and Stefan Kuntz (80th). Karapet Mikaelyan scored a consolation for the home side just before the end.
Ukraine, who beat Portugal on Saturday, stay top of the group but Portugal improved their standing to second with a 3-0 win in Albania.
The Czech Republic, beaten by Germany in final of Euro 96 in June, failed to impose themselves on Spain and the two group six contenders fought out a 0-0 draw in Prague.

England, who lost to Germany in the Euro 96 semifinals, returned to Wembley for the first time since then and came from behind to beat Poland 2-1 thanks to two first half goals from Alan Shearer, the world's costliest player.

Marek Citko shot the Poles ahead after six minutes, but a header from Shearer after 24 minutes and a blistering 18-metre drive 13 minutes later maintained England's 100 per cent start under new coach Glenn Hoddle who admitted afterwards his team had been lucky to survive a second half Polish onslaught.

England stay top of group two on goal difference from Italy, who also made it two wins out of two with their 1-0 victory over Georgia in Perugia. Fabrizio Ravanelli was their match-winner, scoring after 42 minutes.
The two main upsets came in Tel Aviv, where Israel maintained their good start in group five by holding Russia to a 1-1 draw, and in Stockholm, where Austria beat group four leaders Sweden 1-0.
The only goal came after 11 minutes through Andreas Herzog, denting Sweden's 100 percent record and lifting Austria -- temporarily at least -- level on points with Scotland after two games.
Denmark joined Greece level on points at the top of group one after beating the Greeks 2-1 in Copenhagen although Greece stay top on goal difference.
A Theodoros Zagorakis own goal after 25 minutes gave Denmark the lead before Georgios Donis equalised after 35 minutes. Brian Laudrup secured the points for the home side five minutes after halftime.
The most impressive individual scoring burst came from Kjetil Rekdal, who scored a hat-trick in the last seven minutes of a group three match in Oslo to give Norway a 3-0 win over Hungary.
Veteran Tony Cascarino, who did not expect to be playing, took his chance by scoring twice in Ireland's 3-0 win over Macedonia in Dublin.
France, who host the World Cup in two years time, continued their preparations with a convincing 4-0 friendly win over Turkey in Paris.
